This asks a pragma to name a Pylint message by its symbol rather than by its identifier, so it is about how Pylint is configured inside a comment rather than about the code that comment sits beside.

Deciding this needs to know which assignments reach a use, which is a control flow graph rather than a structural one. The kernel builds no basic blocks and no edges between them, so the repository graph records that a name is reached and never in what order.

Deciding this needs the installed environment for a third-party module. For a repository-owned one it needs the resolution outcome of an import binding, which the graph settles internally and no fact family reports, so both halves are missing today and only the second is ever reachable from a repository MCMR never imports.

Deciding this needs the exported names of the module an import reaches, which for anything outside the repository is the installed environment. Inside the repository it needs the resolution outcome of an import binding, which the graph settles internally and no fact family reports. MCMR reads a repository and never imports it.

Deciding this needs the sub-patterns of one `match` case. The neutral vocabulary every frontend fills carries twelve statement kinds and no pattern among them, so a `case` arrives as an unnamed statement with its patterns collapsed into it, and nothing is left to count, to name, or to line up against `__match_args__`.
Deciding this needs the inferred type of an expression. MCMR reads syntax and a resolved graph, so a type checker owns it and the project runs mypy, pyrefly, and ty for exactly this.

Deciding this needs every method of one class at once, because an attribute is only reported where the initializer does not set it too. A syntax fact is one declaration and a class tree stops at the methods that carry their own, so the two halves of that comparison never meet inside one rule.

Deciding this needs a module's own names and one body's local bindings side by side. The symbol family carries module scope, the syntax family carries the body, and a rule receives exactly one family, so neither half can see the other.

Deciding this needs the `global` statement itself, which the neutral vocabulary has no node for and which therefore arrives unnamed, and then the module's own bindings out of a second family to prove the name it declares is missing.

Deciding this needs the parameter kinds of the callee at the call site. A call fact carries the keyword names a caller passes and a handle on the callee, never the signature that handle resolved to, so the keyword and the parameter forbidding it sit in two families.

Deciding this needs the operators of a chained comparison. The neutral vocabulary collapses every comparison, Boolean, unary, and binary expression into one operation node that records no operator, so nothing distinguishes `a < b < c` from `a < b in c`.

Deciding this needs to know that a bare `field` is the one `dataclasses` exports and that the class holding the call is not a dataclass. A syntax tree names a callee as the source spells it, so an imported `field` and a local one read alike, and the decorators of the enclosing class are not beside the call.
